Jordan / Kimberly — thanks, looping in myself as CS lead. Below is a concise validation plan and acceptance checklist we propose. Please review and confirm model variant + any additional constraints.

Proposed validation plan (high level):
1) Smoke (12/03): 30 min, single-region, p95 latency profiler, sanity checks on errors and payload correctness.
2) Warm-up (12/05): repeated ramping with KV cache warm and cold scenarios to measure steady-state behavior.
3) Full load (12/06): sustained 600 rps for 30 minutes, collect token-level latency, CPU/GPU utilization, queue lengths, and tail latencies (p50/p90/p95/p99).
4) Extended run (optional, 12/07): 24h stability run if we see borderline error rates.

Acceptance criteria (mapped):
- Interactive p95 <= 200ms when using gptx-ochre-7b (or a Redwood-verified equivalent) under smoke test assumptions.
- Sustained throughput: 600 rps for 30 min with error rate < 0.5%.
- No single-instance OOM or crash during the full-load test; graceful fallback behavior documented.
- Artifacts: raw logs, per-token latency CSVs, Prometheus/Grafana dashboards, and a short readout deck.

Technical notes / asks from OptiFin:
- Confirm model variant (gptx-ochre-7b or alternate) and quantization preference (8-bit or 4-bit).
- Confirm whether KV cache should be enabled for the full-load run.
- Share any unusual payloads that skew token lengths beyond the spreadsheet.

I will create the shared Drive folder for artifacts and drop a preliminary test harness (link below). If that looks good well lock the windows.

Shared resources: https://drive.redwood.internal/optifin/validation-harness

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

Subject: Re: Inference validation sprint & acceptance criteria — infra notes

Quick infra/ops notes from our side:
- Recommended instance family: g4dn-like GPU pools for initial runs; for sustained 600 rps we recommend 4 x p4d.24xlarge-equivalent hosts behind the routing policy (we'll adjust after smoke).
- Kernel/quantization: start with 8-bit quantized variant for latency/cost tradeoff; run a 4-bit pass only if quality meets thresholds.
- Batching: use dynamic batching to cap latency; target batch size = 8 for the interactive profile, test batch sizes 4/8/16 during warm-up.
- KV cache: run both cold and warm scenarios. Warm cache can improve p95 but must be included in acceptance notes.
- Test harness: were dropping a small script into the Drive: load_test_script.sh (shell script, ~12KB). It wraps the harness, emits per-token latency CSVs, and uploads artifacts to the Drive folder after each run.

Log naming convention: optifin_<run-type>_<YYYYMMDD>_<seq>.zip (contains logs, csvs, prometheus snapshots). We will instrument trace IDs so we can link failing requests back to payloads.

I will be on the smoke window 12/03 and the full run 12/06.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
SRE — Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

Attachment: load_test_script.sh (text, 12KB)
